page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highmem-4 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the n4d server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPU hardware, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Operating with dedicated CPU allocation, the instance ensures consistent compute performance without resource sharing or burstable degradation. The high memory density relative to the vCPU count provides a cost-efficient profile for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing power. By avoiding the overhead of bundled local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators, resource allocation remains focused on memory capacity.

The hardware configuration is suited for memory-intensive applications, small-scale databases, caching layers, and enterprise applications requiring a high RAM-to-vCPU ratio. It also supports lightweight data processing pipelines and backend services where memory capacity is the primary bottleneck rather than raw compute or disk I/O.
